inputs.fetch_note: Read by the pack author at the pinned commit (the v0.23.0 release tag; files verified byte-identical to the inspect_evals 0.23.0 wheel). The dataset revision pin (IFEVAL_DATASET_REVISION) and the record-to-sample mapping are encoded as constants in the builder script. The task's solver is plain generate() (no prompt template). The scorer's delegation to the external instruction_following_eval package is established by ifeval.py itself (require_optional_dependency at task construction and the scorer's imports); that package's code is not part of this pin and not part of the pack's verdict (see the translation notes). Machine-verifiable link is the builder script content hash; this pin is for human audit of those constants.

First 12 rows of the train split (config 'default') via the HuggingFace datasets-server rows API. The hash covers exactly the 12 row payloads consumed (r['row'] per row), as a JSON array in canonical form (keys sorted, compact separators, UTF-8). The dataset revision 966cd89545d6b6acfd7638bc708b98261ca58e84 is pinned in the task source; any upstream change fails this hash loudly.

The translation script for this pack, versioned in this repository (builders/build_ifeval_card.py) alongside the pack, so pack and builder land in one commit; earlier packs pin builders in the evalwarden repo instead. The verifier fetches it from this repository's main branch and verifies it byte-for-byte: the content hash is the pin, and any drift fails loudly. The verifier imports it and runs build_ifeval only.

excluded.item: instruction_id_list and kwargs (the structured list of verifiable instruction ids per prompt and their parameters)
excluded.reason: Harness-side scorer inputs in record_to_sample: they are what the external checker verifies the completion against. The agent sees the instructions only as prose inside the prompt.

translation.notes: The agent prompt is the record's prompt verbatim (plain generate, no template). The pack encodes what the pinned definition establishes: dataset, solver, and the scorer's delegation to the external instruction_following_eval package (test_instruction_following, strict and loose). That package is required at runtime by the task and is NOT version-pinned in the definition, and the scorer additionally downloads NLTK resources at setup; both are stated plainly in the artifact's grader notes and provenance. The verdict covers the definition as pinned, not any particular installed version of the external package.

runs_coverage_note: Definition-level card: no run records exist. Without runs, COST-002..004 and the attempt leg of GRAD-002 cannot fire; without judgments, trajectories, or repeated-run scores, JUDGE-007..009, TRAJ-001..002, NOISE-001..002, and DATA-001..003 stay silent, and GRAD-003 has no declared verifier rule or cached outputs to re-score. JUDGE-001..006 do not apply to the script grader (a deterministic constraint checker, albeit an externally packaged one). The audit correctly stays silent about them. A definition-level card is a floor, not a ceiling.

canonicalization.applies_to: the generated card HTML, before sha256
canonicalization.rule: Two mechanical substitutions: (1) replace <footer>...</footer> with <footer></footer>; (2) replace the methodology-table Generated row timestamp cell with the literal TIMESTAMP. The harness version string is kept: the pack pins the exact version, so a version mismatch must fail, not be normalized away.

repro.command: Save the pack as evidence-pack.json, then run: curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jurayh/evidence-registry/b7d79a06abca949a3abc3ea6dfa51f004e4e6f7f/verify_pack.py -o /tmp/ep_verify.py && python3 /tmp/ep_verify.py evidence-pack.json --work-dir /tmp/ep_work

kill_criterion.question: can a stranger regenerate this card from public inputs?

One disclosed transport substitution in the author run: the builder input was served from the committed file in this repository, because its pinned location is this repo's main-branch raw URL and becomes publicly fetchable with the same commit that lands this pack.
